# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This guide is a companion to the paper

> **Design Effect Ratios for Bayesian Survey Models: A Diagnostic Framework for Identifying Survey-Sensitive Parameters**
> JoonHo Lee, Matthew R. Williams, and Terrance D. Savitsky (2026).

It walks through the code that produces the paper's simulation study and its
empirical application, so that a reader can see exactly how each design was set
up, how it was run, and how the reported numbers and figures were obtained. It
accompanies the replication package at
[github.com/joonho112/svyder-replication](https://github.com/joonho112/svyder-replication)
and the `svyder` R package at
[github.com/joonho112/svyder](https://github.com/joonho112/svyder).

## The idea in one paragraph

When a Bayesian hierarchical model is fit to complex survey data as a weighted
pseudo-posterior, the posterior does not automatically reflect the sampling
design. The usual repair rescales the entire posterior toward a design-based
sandwich variance, but applied to every parameter that is a mistake: a
within-group covariate genuinely needs a wider interval, while a
shrinkage-protected random effect or a between-group coefficient has its
already-narrow interval crushed. The **Design Effect Ratio (DER)** is a
per-parameter diagnostic --- the ratio of a parameter's design-based sandwich
variance to its model-based posterior variance --- that says which is which,
and drives a **compute--classify--correct** workflow that corrects only the
parameters that need it [@LeeWilliamsSavitsky2026].

## What the two studies show

```{r}
#| label: headline
#| echo: false
refit <- readRDS("../data/precomputed/application/nsece_v2_refit.rds")
der_grp <- as.numeric(refit$fit_grp$der)
der_psu <- as.numeric(refit$fit_psu$der)
flag_grp <- sum(der_grp > 1.2)
flag_psu <- sum(der_psu > 1.2)
cells <- readRDS("../data/precomputed/simulation/simulation_cell_summary.rds")
```

The **simulation study** runs a 24-cell factorial design (2,400 fitted models
per structural arm; 4,800 in total) under a genuine two-stage informative
sampling mechanism. Selective correction restores near-nominal coverage of the
exposed within-group coefficient while leaving protected parameters untouched;
the within-group DER separates from every non-target parameter by a factor of
at least 7.1.

The **application** analyzes the 2019 National Survey of Early Care and
Education. Evaluated against the model-group variance target, the diagnostic
flags exactly `r flag_grp` of 54 parameters; evaluated against the design-PSU
target, it flags `r flag_psu`. Every number and figure in this guide is
regenerated from the results shipped with the package --- the two counts above
are computed live from `nsece_v2_refit.rds`.

## Two ways to reproduce

The package supports two tracks. **Track A** reruns everything from the
beginning: the simulation on synthetic data, and the application on the
restricted-use NSECE files. **Track B** regenerates every figure and table in
minutes from the shipped, non-identifiable results, with no restricted data and
no Stan. This guide is written from the Track B perspective; the Track A
scripts are described alongside so you can see the full computation.

::: {.callout-note}
Theory is stated here only to the depth needed to read the code. For the
definitions, theorems, and proofs, see the paper [@LeeWilliamsSavitsky2026].
:::
